_what_this_is: The DEFINITION OF DONE for bin/wrought-scope, and the only hand-authored file in this
directory -- index/scope-index.json beside it is GENERATED and must never be hand-edited.
Each query names the files a session MUST be given for that task. The tool passes only if it
returns every one of them inside the cap, and only if the set it returns is far smaller than
the tree it was selected from. Run: bin/test-wrought-scope
TWO THINGS ABOUT HOW THIS FILE WAS BUILT, because a fixture set that was tuned to the tool it
grades is not a test, it is a mirror:
1. The first three queries and their must-include sets are the DISPATCHING PROMPT'S, taken
verbatim. They were not chosen by whoever wrote the ranker.
2. The other twenty came in TWO batches and the second batch is a weaker claim than the
first, so both are stated rather than averaged. Ten were written by reading the repo-map
and docs/ before any ranking measurement existed. TEN MORE WERE ADDED PART-WAY THROUGH
THE PARAMETER SWEEP, because thirteen fixtures were visibly too few to choose between
ranking configurations without fitting them -- they were written to widen the target,
not to hit it, and none was altered after seeing how it scored. That is still weaker
than a held-out set and the report says so under WHAT THIS DID NOT ESTABLISH: the
tuning set and the grading set are the SAME 23 queries, so generalization beyond them
is UNMEASURED.
3. ONE fixture was corrected after measuring, recorded here rather than quietly fixed:
'offline wheel install and supply chain' originally named bin/secpack-fetch, which the
tool ranked 24th and which is about pinning security TOOLS. bin/secpack-freeze is the
file that freezes the offline wheel set, the tool ranked it 5th, and THE FIXTURE WAS
WRONG, NOT THE TOOL. It is corrected here and the original error is on the record.
_cap_is_uniform_and_deliberate: ONE cap for every query, never a per-query cap. A per-query cap is how a failing fixture
becomes a passing one without the tool changing, and this file would then measure nothing.
25 of 154 indexed files is 16% of the tree by count and far less by token cost, which is the
number that actually matters and which the test prints.
AT THE DEFAULT CAP OF 12 the tool returns 33 of these 34 must-include files; the one that
needs the wider cap is src/wrought_verifier/__main__.py on 'oracle verdict logic', reached at
rank 22 through the dependency graph rather than by any word it contains. That is stated here
so the gap is a measurement rather than a discovery.

_symbols_assert_containment: `defined_in` must be AMONG the files the tool reports as defining the symbol, not the only
one. `classify` is genuinely defined twice -- src/wrought_supervisor/classify.py and a
same-named helper in bin/wrought-runner -- and a test demanding uniqueness would be demanding
the tool lie about the tree.
